title: Conceptual Mathematics: A First Introduction to Categories
byline: F. William Lawvere and Stephen H. Schanuel · Cambridge University Press, 2nd edition 2009
note: Tests, quizzes and short summary pages between sessions are not broken out. Summaries are in our own words; the text stays in the PDF.
summary: A gentle first course in category theory that assumes only high-school algebra, built from “Articles” that set out ideas and classroom “Sessions” that work through them with students. Starting from sets and maps, it develops composition, isomorphisms, sections, retractions and idempotents (with Brouwer’s fixed-point theorem as an application), then categories of structured sets such as endomaps, dynamical systems and graphs, universal mapping properties (terminal and initial objects, products, sums, distributive and linear categories), and finally exponentials, cartesian closed categories, subobjects, truth values and toposes.
